# Navimower Map Card 0.3.7-beta13

## Prepared short-tail transport

This prerelease completes the frontend side of the beta25 Prepared Render Model
efficiency change.

With Navimower 0.4.5-beta25+, the card no longer needs the full raw active trail
on every normal Map API refresh once the backend short-tail capability has been
discovered.

### Single mower

- The first map load remains a full legacy-compatible request so cold startup
  always has a complete fallback.
- After beta25 capability discovery, subsequent Map API requests opt into
  `prepared_live_tail_only=1`.
- The prepared SVG resource remains the authoritative route backbone.
- `prepared_live_tail.segments` supplies only the points after that backbone.
- New Home Assistant/MQTT position points continue locally after the backend
  short tail, so the visible trail remains connected to the live mower marker.
- A short tail is accepted only when its `base_resource_id` matches the loaded
  prepared live resource and its trail session is compatible.
- If the backend publishes a new prepared backbone, a changed
  `base_resource_id` forces an immediate manifest/resource refresh.
- Older integrations or unusable short-tail responses keep the beta12 raw-trail
  fallback.

### Prepared manifest cadence

Beta13 reads `live_route_min_interval_s` advertised by the integration.

With Navimower 0.4.5-beta25 this means normal live manifest checks are throttled
to 30 seconds instead of being attempted on every MQTT trail update. Lifecycle
changes and a short-tail/resource identity mismatch still bypass the normal
cadence.

The mower marker itself is unchanged and continues to update from Home
Assistant/MQTT in real time.

### Multi mower

- Non-anchor member map requests also switch to
  `prepared_live_tail_only=1` after capability discovery.
- Member rendering consumes the backend short-tail object when it matches the
  currently loaded prepared resource.
- A tail referencing a newer resource forces immediate prepared-resource
  adoption.
- The anchor member reuses the Single card's already-loaded prepared live
  resource instead of starting a separate 30-second adoption window.
- Older/full-trail member payloads keep the previous beta12 fallback.

### Safety

The frontend never assumes that a tail belongs to the currently rendered
backbone. Resource id and trail-session compatibility are checked before the
short-tail path is used.

If beta25 reports the tail unusable, it keeps the raw trail in the response and
beta13 falls back to the existing renderer.

History/session archives, current-cycle zone artifacts, mower controls, Schedule
and static geometry behavior are unchanged.

## Regression coverage

The beta13 regression verifies:

- beta25 short-tail capability discovery;
- `prepared_live_tail_only=1` request construction;
- backend-advertised 30-second manifest cadence;
- short-tail/resource-id alignment;
- MQTT continuation after the backend tail;
- immediate detection of a newer backbone id;
- fallback request behavior for older integrations;
- Multi short-tail wiring and anchor prepared-resource reuse.

## Recommended field test

Use Navimower 0.4.5-beta25 with Map Card 0.3.7-beta13 while mowing.

Expected integration diagnostics:

- `live_prepare_min_interval_s: 30.0`;
- `live_build_count` grows roughly at the 30-second cadence during ordinary
  mowing, with immediate extra publications only around lifecycle transitions;
- `manifest_reads` grows much more slowly than with beta12;
- `live_resource_bytes_served_total` measures actual prepared resource bodies
  sent to the frontend;
- `live_tail_requests > 0`;
- `live_tail_success_count > 0`;
- `live_tail_full_fallback_count` stays low/zero during normal mowing;
- `last_live_tail_point_count` remains small compared with the full active
  route point count;
- all prepared-render failure counters remain zero.

Visually, mower movement and the newest trail should remain continuous while the
prepared SVG backbone updates only about every 30 seconds.
